Aditya / Marissa —

Adding technical notes for the workbook and proposed log excerpts:

- Detection scope: we run multi-stage signals (pattern-based, model-scored classifier, anomaly detectors) that trigger a "flag" entity persisted in the audit store. Flags include classification label, confidence, model-version, and routing decision.
- Detection latency: classification and flag emission occur inline within 40-120ms P95 for standard gen requests; longer for 100k+ token contexts.
- Enforcement: policy decisions are surfaced as policy actions in the API response header (policy_action: allow|warn|block) and as event records in the audit log. Customers can configure automatic blocking, soft-warning (allow + metadata), or operator review.
- Audit trails & access: immutable event store with HMAC-backed indexing; queryable via Console or an authenticated API, with role-based access controls (RBAC) and fine-grained query logging.
- Evidence plan: we'll provide a redacted log excerpt that preserves timestamps, flags, model-ids and response latencies; sensitive user text will be redacted.
- Escalations: playbook ties automated flags -> CS triage queue -> security on-call; timeline targets: Triage within 1 hour (business hours), Investigation initial findings within 24 hours.

I'll prepare the log excerpt and a short architecture diagram showing where detection sits in the request flow.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Security & Applied ML
